name: Pairwise Comparison and Forced Ranking
diagnostic: Flat-priority list paralysis. Lists where every item is labeled "High Priority" create triage deadlock because relative values remain unexamined.

procedure.text: List the competing priorities, no more than eight.
Compare two at a time: if only one could ship, which is more critical?
Run every pairing and tally head-to-head wins.
Sort by total wins for a forced order with no ties.

trap: Letting circular preferences stall the process (A beats B, B beats C, C beats A); impose a strict criterion.
procedureFull:
1. Extract an unranked set of competing candidate priorities (limit to N ≤ 8 items).
2. Construct a tournament bracket or pairwise matrix: compare Item 1 against Item 2 in isolation, asking: "If I could only deliver one of these two, which is non-negotiably more critical?"
3. Iterate through all combinations (N(N-1) ÷ 2 pairings), tallying head-to-head victories for each item.
4. Sort the list strictly by total win count, yielding an absolute, forced-ranked sequence free of tied priorities.
setupFull: Items: [A: Security Patch, B: New Feature, C: Refactor Auth, D: Documentation] A vs B -> A wins | A vs C -> A wins | A vs D -> A wins (A: 3 wins) B vs C -> C wins | B vs D -> B wins (B: 1 win) C vs D -> C wins (C: 2 wins) Forced Priority Order: 1. A, 2. C, 3. B, 4. D
trapFull: Allowing circular trade-off debates to stall the process (e.g., choosing A over B, B over C, and C over A). The operator must impose strict, transitive decision criteria.
